note: The OLG adequately covers all three core requirements of FNS 1021. (1) Verification of wages: The 'Types of Earned Income > Verification of Income' section states earned income is mandatory verification, must display gross wages and hours worked, and lists acceptable documents (pay stubs, pay envelopes, employer statements). (2) Questioning and documenting earnings: The OLG covers this across multiple pages — workers must consult households about hourly/piecework income expectations ('Types of Earned Income > Income from Hourly and Piecework Employment'), must ask clarifying questions about stipends vs. wages, and the Interim Report procedures require detailed follow-up on earned income changes including cold-calling clients and sending VC-1s when verification is inconsistent. The Narratives Guidelines checklist requires documenting income verification. (3) Investigating when expenses exceed income: The OLG has a dedicated cross-program policy called SLAM (Suspected Living Above Means) under 'Cross Programs > SLAM > Addressing SLAM' that explicitly requires workers to explore how households are meeting expenses when reported expenses exceed income, including asking clarifying questions about subsidized costs, unreported income, and split expenses. The 'Verification of Dependent Care Expenses' section also flags the expenses-exceed-income scenario as triggering additional verification. The L1 finding that the expense-to-income investigation mandate was missing appears to have been based on incomplete search results — the SLAM policy directly implements this FNS requirement.
